methodology_note: NZ general insurer. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md (insurer -> BVPS compounding x exit P/B). Owner-FCF DCF is invalid: reported FCF (NZ$121.7m FY25, NZ$-11.2m FY23) is float/claims-reserve/investment-portfolio timing, not owner earnings, and the balance sheet has no borrowings to net. Model: project book value per share from a scenario ROE path net of dividends (60-80% payout policy), apply an exit P/B to Year-5 BVPS, discount dividends plus terminal value at a NZD cost of equity. Same family as FRFHF (BVPS compounding), SRBK (residual income) and SUM.NZ (capitalised earnings).

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares at 31-Mar-2026 (346.47m: 343.41m on issue + ~3.1m executive share rights), held FLAT: SBC (NZ$0.7m FY25) is expensed in NPAT and the rights are already in the diluted count. The March-2025 NZ$45.5m compulsory capital return cancelled 38.06m shares (379.48m -> 342.55m), so per-share history across FY2024/FY2025 is not comparable.
inputs.bvps_start_note: 31-Mar-2026 equity NZ$318.1m / 346.47m diluted = NZ$0.9180, rolled to 30-Sep-2026 (FY26E) by +H2 FY26 reported NPAT est NZ$18.0m (underlying ~NZ$23m = guidance midpoint NZ$60m less H1 NZ$36.8m, less ~NZ$5m non-underlying) and -5c interim dividend (NZ$17.2m) = NZ$318.9m -> NZ$0.9204. Y1 = FY2027.
inputs.total_debt_note: No borrowings; IFRS-16 lease liabilities only. NOT subtracted: the model values equity directly (dividends + exit P/B at cost of equity).
inputs.last_fcf_label: FY2026E reported NPAT (H1 actual 22.9 + H2 est 18.0). For an insurer NPAT is the owner flow; reported FCF is investment/float timing.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 as reported (OCF 143.8 - capex 22.1). Not used.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report note 8.5 (line 3378): share-based payment expense NZ$0.7m (FY24 NZ$0.4m). Already expensed in NPAT under IFRS 2; dilution inside diluted share count.
inputs.interest_income_note: Investment income on the NZ$326m fixed-interest portfolio is core insurer earnings and stays inside NPAT; it is not stripped as it would be in an owner-FCF model.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 compulsory capital return (scheme of arrangement, Mar-2025). No buyback in H1 FY26; solvency margin NZ$90.1m vs NZ$84.3m internal target leaves ~NZ$6m of surplus, so no further capital return is modelled.
inputs.dividend_policy: 60-80% of adjusted earnings where prudent; FY25 total 24.5c (8c interim + 7.5c ordinary final + 9c special from unused large-event allowance); FY26 interim 5c.
inputs.ifrs17_note: FY2024 onward reports under IFRS 17 (insurance revenue); FY2022-FY2023 are IFRS 4 and not comparable on the revenue line. Equity and NPAT are comparable enough for ROE.
inputs.notes: MODEL: BVPS compounding x exit P/B at cost of equity (insurer row of the dcf-methods routing table). No prior DCF for this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry. Cost of equity built in NZD: NZ 10-yr government ~4.4% (Sep-2026 estimate, RBNZ easing cycle) + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.05 + ~0.8% small-cap/catastrophe-concentration premium = ~11% base (bull 10%, bear 12.5%). Price is a regular NZX close, not after-hours. The dashboard slider engine has no BVPS mode: expect `slider engine ... FALLBACK` for this ticker exactly as for FRFHF/SRBK; the JSON values are produced by assumptions[scenario] via the formulas in TWR.NZ_DCF_Model.xlsx.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case BVPS CAGR net of dividends (0.92 -> 1.17 over FY26E-FY31, ~5%/yr), approximating GWP growth; used only as the PEG proxy
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every trailing CAGR describes a turnaround, not a trend: FY2022 was a weak year (NPAT NZ$18.9m), FY2023 a catastrophe loss (NZ$-1.2m; Auckland floods + Cyclone Gabrielle, NZ$38m large events) and FY2024-25 benign weather years (large events NZ$0 and NZ$7.2m vs NZ$45-50m allowances). EPS 3yr CAGR 70% and FCF 3yr CAGR 46% are meaningless; equity CAGR 3.4% is depressed by the NZ$45.5m capital return; revenue CAGR 13% straddles the IFRS 4 -> IFRS 17 break. Five-year figures are unavailable (Metrics.csv starts FY2022). Base case is anchored on FY26 guidance and a mid-cycle ROE, not on any CAGR.
historical_growth.historical_pb_note: P/B = Yahoo NZX close at 30-Sep / basic BVPS. Re-rating from ~0.9x (FY22-23, ROE <6%) to 1.6-1.8x (FY24-25, ROE 21-25%) and 2.1x today tracks the ROE step-up; before FY2022 Tower traded ~0.8-1.1x book for years.

base.description: Mid-cycle reported ROE 16-17%: underlying NPAT ~NZ$58-65m (FY26 guidance NZ$55-65m carried forward with the NZ$45m large-event allowance treated as fully used every year), GWP +4-5%/yr (below the >7.5% FY28 target after the in-year cut to low-single-digit), MER drifting to ~30% (management targets 28-30% by FY28), BAU claims ratio normalising toward 47-48%, FY26 reinsurance saving (10.7% of GWP) retained, ~NZ$5m/yr of non-underlying leakage (remediation/regulatory) persists. 70% payout of reported NPAT (policy: 60-80% of adjusted earnings). Exit P/B 1.6x = (ROE 16% - g 3%)/(CoE 11% - 3%), inside the FY22-FY26 realised range 0.87x-2.14x.
base.terminal_growth_note: No perpetuity growth: terminal value is exit P/B x Year-5 BVPS (explicit judgement), consistent with a fundamental P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) at g ~3%.

bull.description: Management hits its FY28 targets (GWP >NZ$750m, MER 28-30%, COR 85-87%) with the Westpac (Jul-2026) and Kiwibank back-book partnerships delivering, weather at or below allowance, reinsurance staying soft; reported ROE 19-21%, underlying NPAT NZ$70-85m. Exit P/B 2.1x = about today's multiple and the top of Tower's realised range; the fundamental (ROE 20%, g 3.5%, CoE 10%) formula gives 2.5x, deliberately capped.
bull.terminal_growth_note: No perpetuity growth: terminal value is exit P/B x Year-5 BVPS (explicit judgement), consistent with a fundamental P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) at g ~3%.

bear.description: FY27 is a large-event year exceeding the allowance (FY23 precedent: NZ$38m net plus inflated BAU claims -> ROE ~0%; modelled 8%), followed by a structurally lower mid-cycle: BAU claims ratio 50%, reinsurance market re-hardens toward 13% of GWP, MER stuck at 31%, investment income lower, further conduct costs. Reported ROE 10-11%, roughly at cost of equity, so exit P/B 0.9x (FY22-FY23 year-end multiples 0.87x-0.90x). Payout at the 60% policy floor.
bear.terminal_growth_note: No perpetuity growth: terminal value is exit P/B x Year-5 BVPS (explicit judgement), consistent with a fundamental P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) at g ~3%.

base.fcf_label: dividend_per_share (equity flow; NPAT retained compounds BVPS)

bull.fcf_label: dividend_per_share (equity flow; NPAT retained compounds BVPS)

bear.fcf_label: dividend_per_share (equity flow; NPAT retained compounds BVPS)

entry_price.method: Year-5 terminal value (exit P/B x BVPS, an explicit judgement so not rebuilt at the hurdle) plus dividends reinvested at the hurdle, discounted 5 years at 15%. Exit-multiple model (exit_pb).

required_return_table.note: Base ROE/payout path and exit P/B 1.6x held; only the discount rate varies. The 11% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = cost of equity 9-13%, columns = exit P/B 1.2x-2.0x applied to Year-5 BVPS, base ROE path [16,17,17,16.5,16]% and 70% payout held. Field names wacc_range/terminal_growth_range retained for dashboard compatibility; the column axis is exit P/B, not perpetuity growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% house default): a NZ/Pacific-concentrated catastrophe book where one FY23-style year zeroes earnings, plus a conduct record (NZ$7m FMA penalty, ~NZ$12m remediation) and an in-year GWP guidance cut. Bull 30%: the FY28 targets are management's own and the Westpac/Kiwibank channels are contracted, but the >7.5% GWP CAGR looks stretched after low-single-digit FY26.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC-zero market (NZ$0.7m expense, inside NPAT and the diluted count): house and street bases coincide, so the band collapses and band_position is null.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Tower is a short-tail general insurer: value is the stream of underwriting and investment earnings on a regulated capital base, paid out at 60-80% and compounding the remainder into book. The model projects book value per share from a reported-ROE path net of dividends, capitalises Year-5 book at an exit P/B tied to (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) and bounded by Tower's own realised range (0.87x-2.14x), and discounts dividends plus terminal value at an NZD cost of equity. No enterprise value, no net debt, no WACC.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_fcf_dcf: Reported FCF swings from NZ$-11m (FY23) to NZ$125m (FY24) on claims-reserve, reinsurance-recovery and investment-portfolio timing; FY25 OCF of NZ$144m against NPAT of NZ$84m is float, not distributable cash. Tower has no borrowings, so net debt is meaningless, and EBITDA does not exist for an insurer under IFRS 17.
valuation_philosophy.mid_cycle_earnings: FY26 guidance (underlying NPAT NZ$55-65m) assumes the NZ$45m large-event allowance is fully used; the actual four-year average large-event cost is ~NZ$19m (FY23 38, FY24 0, FY25 7.2, FY26 ytd 23.5), so 'allowance fully used' is a conservative mid-cycle, not a benign one. The base case carries that level forward with modest GWP growth and MER improvement, a BAU claims ratio normalising to 47-48% (from 38% in H1 FY25 and 44% in H1 FY26), and ~NZ$5m/yr of non-underlying leakage. FY24-25 reported ROE of 21-25% was benign-weather peak and is not extrapolated; FY23's ~0% is the bear's Year 1.
valuation_philosophy.cost_of_equity_basis: NZD: NZ 10-yr ~4.4% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.05 + ~0.8% small-cap/catastrophe premium = 11% base; 10% bull; 12.5% bear.
valuation_philosophy.exit_multiple_basis: Fundamental P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g), g = 3%: base 1.6x, bull 2.5x capped at 2.1x (today's multiple, top of history), bear 0.86x rounded to 0.9x (FY22-23 year-end multiples).
valuation_philosophy.what_would_change_the_view: Upside: FY27 large events well under allowance with the special-dividend pattern repeating; MER at 28-30% by FY28; GWP tracking the >7.5% CAGR. Downside: a large event exceeding reinsurance retention; reinsurance renewal (Oct) re-hardening above 12% of GWP; further FMA/CoFI findings; BAU claims ratio above 48%.
